responseBody.summary: This server hosts PURL resources: addressable, versioned, stateful objects whose operations, authority and history are machine-discoverable. Start at a resource URL with Accept: application/purl+json, then GET its manifest.

representations.use: human visualisation; embeds the JSON representation

authentication.note: Tokens identify a principal on this instance. They do not prove anything about the underlying person, agent or model.

vocabulary.name: Programmable URL Protocol
vocabulary.thesis: A URL can address a stateful resource and the operations on it — with authority, provenance and continuity explicit — rather than only a document.

layers.transport: URLs, HTTP methods, content negotiation, manifests, HTML/JSON representations.
layers.continuity: Resources as hash-chained event logs; ownership, grants and delegation chains; checkpoints, handoff, fork, merge, supersession, lifecycle.
layers.research: Projection of event logs (or any sequence) into symbol sequences; measures, transition graphs, grammar compression, surrogate tests, reproducible experiment records.

rights.observe: See that the resource exists, its metadata, manifest and event headers (no payloads).
rights.read: See full state, collections, grants, event payloads, checkpoints and diffs.
rights.append: Add entries to collections (findings, annotations, checkpoints, acknowledgements). Never removes or edits.
rights.update: Change the free-form state object (JSON Merge Patch).
rights.assign: Change who is responsible for continuing the work (assignee). Never changes ownership.
rights.link: Record typed relations from this resource to others (references, supersedes, merged_from).
rights.lifecycle: Move the resource through its lifecycle (close, complete, cancel, reopen, archive, restore).
rights.grant: Issue grants of rights the holder already has (attenuation), and revoke grants descending from them.

administrator.note: instance-scoped; cannot read or edit content

properties: commutative (as a set keyed by entry id)

operations.description: Current representation. Content is redacted to what your rights allow; the representation says what was redacted.

operations.description: Alias of inspect.

operations.name: diff
operations.description: Structural differences between two versions (JSON Pointer paths).

operations.name: history
operations.description: Event log. Observers see headers; readers see payloads.

operations.name: state_at
operations.description: State reconstructed by replaying the log to a version.

operations.name: lineage
operations.description: Ancestors, descendants, supersession and merge relations.

operations.name: verify
operations.description: Replay the log and check the hash chain and every state hash.

operations.name: continuity
operations.description: Latest checkpoint package plus everything that changed since it.

operations.name: synchronize
operations.description: Fetch events after the version you hold; apply them with the reducer to catch up.

operations.name: subscribe
operations.description: Server-Sent Events stream of new events (Last-Event-ID = version).

operations.description: Create a resource; the caller becomes its owner.
